text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week decline of 14%, as refineries across the U.S. operate at high utilization (95.7%) while oil inventories remain elevated at 694 million barrels. High refinery rates combined with plentiful supply typically compress profit margins—refiners make money when they can process cheap crude into higher-value products, but that advantage shrinks when crude is abundant and storage is full.

The broader headwind is energy transition risk. This week's climate summit collapse removed a potential floor under fossil fuel prices, and multiple news stories highlight how capital is rotating toward clean energy infrastructure (quantum computing for grid optimization, hydrogen catalysts) and toward companies positioning themselves as energy providers for AI rather than traditional oil and gas. For a refiner dependent on the crude-to-products spread, that sentiment shift matters as much as today's inventory levels.
